Khaby Lame.text: He started posting on TikTok after being laid off from his job as a factory CNC machine operator in 2020.
Khaby Lame.evidence: Lame worked as a CNC machine operator at a factory near Turin, before getting laid off in March 2020. After Lame was laid off during the COVID-19 pandemic, he began posting on TikTok.

Charli D'Amelio.text: In 2022 she won season 31 of Dancing with the Stars, partnered with Mark Ballas.
Charli D'Amelio.evidence: In 2022, D'Amelio won the thirty-first season of the dance competition series Dancing with the Stars alongside Mark Ballas.

MrBeast.text: His productions got far more extravagant after a 2017 video of him counting to 100,000 drew tens of thousands of views.
MrBeast.evidence: In January 2017, after his video "I Counted to 100,000!" drew tens of thousands of views within days, his productions quickly became more extravagant.

TikTok.text: Though made in China, the app is blocked in mainland China, where Douyin is available instead.
TikTok.evidence: Despite being a Chinese-made app, TikTok is blocked in mainland China and Hong Kong, and Douyin is available there instead.

Bella Poarch.text: She is a U.S. Navy veteran who enlisted at 17 and became an aviation ordnanceman.
Bella Poarch.evidence: Poarch is a United States Navy veteran, enlisting in the Navy at 17, and becoming an aviation ordnanceman in 2017.

Addison Rae.text: She was studying broadcast journalism at LSU to become a sports broadcaster when TikTok took off.
Addison Rae.evidence: Before moving to Los Angeles to pursue her career, she briefly attended Louisiana State University (LSU) where she studied broadcast journalism in the fall to become a sports broadcaster but then dropped out when she began to gain popularity on TikTok.

Zach King.text: His 2011 video Jedi Kittens, two kittens fighting with lightsabers, got over a million views in three days.
Zach King.evidence: In 2011, he posted a video titled Jedi Kittens on YouTube that he produced with a college friend under the name FinalCutKing. The video showed two kittens fighting with lightsabers. The video gained over a million views in three days and went on to have over 25 million views as of March 2025.

FIFA World Cup.text: An estimated 3.57 billion people, close to half the world's population, watched the 2018 tournament.
FIFA World Cup.evidence: The viewership of the 2018 World Cup was estimated to be 3.57 billion, close to half of the global population, while the engagement with the 2022 World Cup was estimated to be 5 billion, with about 1.5 billion people watching the final match.

Kimberly Loaiza.text: In 2020 she launched a clothing line and opened her own telephone company.
Kimberly Loaiza.evidence: In 2020, Loaiza launched a clothing line, opened her own telephone company, broke the record of the most subscribers on YouTube for Spanish-speakers, and collaborated with other social media personalities such as James Charles.
